# Estate attorney transition (keywords: Stephanie retiring, March 2025, new attorney, Montserrat, probate, handover)

## 2024-11-12: Stephanie retiring March 2025
- Crystal says Stephanie revealed she is retiring in March 2025. Crystal is worried about probate and needs a NEW estate attorney to make sure the estate plan is in order.
- Context from profile file: Stephanie is (a) the "attorney" who reviewed the will (2024-05-01), (b) the named guardian for Francis and Michael, (c) a friend. Her review was never independent. Her credentials and Montserrat admission were never verified. No written opinion on record.
- Implication: retirement removes the attorney from the picture before the will is confirmed executed (last known status: not executed as of 2024-08-10; 90% self-reported). Treat the new independent Montserrat attorney as the priority, not a replacement for Stephanie as guardian nominee (she stays a separate question).
- Crystal's own guardian choice for Francis/Michael (Stephanie, alternate Kevin) still needs re-confirmation with the new attorney, because Stephanie's acceptance is unconfirmed.

## Plan given (2024-11-12)
1. Ask Stephanie for the complete file in writing before she leaves: drafts, notes, any opinion, the 2024-05-01 review, the probate-timeline source, the affidavit list. Request a written handover note on what is done and what is open.
2. Ask Stephanie to state in writing: her Montserrat admission (bar number/year), whether she is retiring from practice fully, and who can take over questions after March.
3. Find an independent Montserrat-qualified estate/probate attorney. Not Stephanie, not Kevin (paralegal, alternate executor/guardian), not Douglas, not Dwayne. Check sources: Montserrat Bar / Eastern Caribbean legal directories, referrals from Christina (accountant) only as a lead, verify licence independently. (Verification details not confirmed from here.)
4. Questions for candidate attorneys: Montserrat call and years of practice; probate and guardianship experience; will execution formalities (witnesses, electronic wills/e-signatures); fee structure (fixed vs hourly); conflict check; whether they will issue a written opinion on the will; experience with film/TV rights, royalties, production company shares; whether US-side advice is needed (memory notes US tax references); who the client is (Crystal only).
5. Engagement letter in Crystal's name only. Non-beneficiaries and non-executors handle logistics only.
6. Hand the new attorney: signed-or-unsigned will text (no access codes), asset list, guardian nominations, Stephanie's handover note, tax summary from Christina, appraisal (home $365,000 as of 2024-08-04).
7. Prioritize execution before March 2025 if possible; do not set a timeline for probate outcomes until the Montserrat attorney confirms the process. Probate durations quoted so far (6-9 months, then 5-7 months) remain unverified.

## Open items to ask Crystal
- Has any version of the will actually been signed and witnessed? Where is any original?
- Did Stephanie ever issue written advice or a Montserrat-law opinion?
- Is the Stephanie who is retiring the same Stephanie as the 2024-03-22 estate-tax meeting?
- Which accountant/advisor she consulted (Christina?) and any written summary.

## 2024-11-12: review timing, Aug 5 update, affidavits (keywords: September 15, review, affidavits, Aug 5, 10%)
- Crystal asks whether to review the will again "before September 15." That date has PASSED (today is 2024-11-12). Earlier notes had the final review as 2024-09-15 and also 2024-10-15 (unconfirmed). Ask whether any review happened.
- Aug 5 "10% increase" to children's inheritance still ambiguous (+10 points vs +10% relative). Only a signed, witnessed version counts; if the Aug 5 version was never executed, the prior executed version (if any) governs. Ask Crystal to confirm.
- Stephanie advised notarized guardianship affidavits to speed probate court approval. Not verified; Stephanie conflicted and retiring March 2025. Advice: independent Montserrat attorney must confirm which affidavits, who signs, content, notary; affidavits must be accurate and based on personal knowledge; no backdating; no speed guarantee. Don't draft or sign until confirmed.
- Reminder: remove access codes from the will (Aug 6 issue) and confirm no unsigned drafts with codes are shared.
- Advice: review now with the new independent attorney, not on a Sept 15 date; bring: current will text, Aug 5 and Aug 7 changes, Stephanie handover note, affidavit list, asset list, guardian acceptances.

## 2024-11-12: parents' care fund (keywords: care fund, $7,000, Kimberly, Bradley, parents' care)
- Crystal added a $7,000 care fund for parents Kimberly (74) and Bradley (79) in will updates on 2024-11-01. Earlier planning figure was $100,000 (proposed, March 2024). Conflict: which figure is current? Also not known whether the Nov 1 update is signed/witnessed.
- Crystal asks if $7,000 is enough. Cannot judge without: parents' care needs and health, care setting (home vs facility), local monthly costs in Montserrat (not verified), parents' own income and savings, home/property ownership, whether parents want the fund, and whether they have their own wills/POA.
- Sizing method given: (monthly care cost x expected months of care) + one-off costs (equipment, home changes, transport, respite, emergencies) + contingency, minus parents' own income and assets available. Figures to come from local quotes, not assumed.
- Advice: parents decide their own care and POA/wills; fund held in a separate account or trust with a trustee other than Douglas unless disclosed and checked; written terms from the independent Montserrat attorney; Christina to check tax on gifts/fund.

## 2024-11-12: parents' needs exceed fund; separate trust? (keywords: parents trust, lifetime trust, testamentary, care costs)
- Crystal asks whether to set up a separate trust if parents' needs exceed $7,000.
- Key point given: a will-based fund only pays after Crystal's death and probate, so it cannot pay for parents' care while Crystal is alive. A lifetime (inter vivos) trust or a funded account is the relevant tool for current care.
- Options to review with independent Montserrat attorney and Christina: lifetime trust for parents' care (funded now; trustee not Douglas unless disclosed); larger testamentary fund in will (after death only); parents' own resources and POA; care insurance if available in Montserrat; gifts during life (tax and liquidity checks).
- Cautions: parents must consent and decide their own care; Crystal's own liquidity must not be impaired; trust terms and tax unverified for Montserrat; no setup until attorney advice.

## 2024-11-12: tax implications of funding parents' trust (keywords: gift tax, income tax, capital gains, grantor, revocable, exclusion)
- Crystal asks what tax implications to expect when funding a parents' care trust. Montserrat tax rules NOT verified; no assumption made.
- General points given: (1) gift tax on transfers to trust, rules depend on jurisdiction; US annual exclusion 2024 is $18,000 per recipient if any US rules apply; (2) revocable vs irrevocable: assets in revocable trust usually still in estate; irrevocable may leave estate; (3) income tax on trust income, grantor vs separate trust; (4) capital gains on transfer of appreciated assets (equipment, film rights, shares) if applicable; (5) parents' own tax and public-benefit eligibility if trust pays their care; (6) record keeping, valuation of non-cash assets; (7) Christina's Aug 3 advice still unverified; equipment sale conflict unresolved.
- Advice: written tax memo from Christina and the independent Montserrat attorney before funding; confirm which jurisdictions apply (Crystal, parents, trust, assets); don't transfer until confirmed.

## 2024-11-12: digital legacy update Nov 5 (keywords: Instagram, TikTok, $800, legacy contact, memorialization, monetized accounts)
- Crystal updated will on 2024-11-05 with digital legacy provisions for Instagram and TikTok, "valued at $800 combined." Asks what else to consider. Unknown: whether Nov 5 update is printed, signed, witnessed (likely digital, so no legal effect until executed); how $800 was derived; any monetization (creator payouts, brand deals) on these accounts.
- Points given: social accounts usually can't be transferred as property; platform terms govern; use each platform's legacy/memorialization/deletion options (check current settings, not verified here); no passwords or access codes in will; executor access letter and password manager with emergency access outside will; list monetized accounts with payout details and contracts; separate film/TV rights, royalties, and content copyrights from social accounts; 2FA recovery contacts; attorney review of the will text; ask versions of apps/tools (preference).
- Also: Sept 20 digital asset review outcome unknown; ask.

## 2024-11-12: organizing binder (financial statements, insurance; target Dec 1) (keywords: binder, beneficiary designations, insurance, probate assets, asset list)
- Crystal started gathering financial statements and insurance policies on 2024-11-03; target full binder by 2024-12-01.
- Explained: will only controls probate assets. Joint-ownership property, beneficiary-designated accounts/policies, and trust assets pass outside the will, so designations must match will intent (minors cannot receive directly; use trust or guardian-controlled designation). Mortgage/liens reduce net estate; percentages apply to net estate. Film/TV rights, royalties, company shares need valuation. Liquidity needed for probate costs and care fund.
- Binder: index of each asset, owner, title, beneficiary, value date, account access location (no passwords in binder copies marked as copies); originals kept in safe per attorney advice; share only information copies (Stephanie/Douglas) per safe plan.
- Advice: bring binder to independent Montserrat attorney; Dec 1 is a personal target, not a legal deadline; the binder doesn't change the will until a new version is signed and witnessed.
- Open: existing insurance policies' beneficiaries; whether home is jointly owned; mortgage balance; whether $3,000 life insurance was bought.

## 2024-11-12: Diana confirms e-signatures accepted in Montserrat (keywords: Diana, electronic signature, e-will, Nov 10, verify)
- Crystal says new attorney Diana confirmed on 2024-11-10 that Montserrat now accepts electronic will signatures, a change "since July 2024." NOT verified by me. Diana's independence, admission, and fee arrangement not yet recorded.
- Implications to check: (1) whether the rule covers wills (vs general e-signatures), statute/citation and effective date; (2) whether witnesses must be physically present or can witness electronically; (3) execution platform requirements, identity verification, audit trail, tamper-evident copy; (4) which original counts (electronic original vs paper), storage and custody (safe plan changes); (5) revocation of prior versions (Aug 5, Nov 1, Nov 5 digital updates; earlier paper or WillMaker drafts); (6) whether a previously signed paper will is affected; (7) guardianship affidavits and notarization still need the separate rules; (8) executors' access to e-originals in probate court.
- Advice: ask Diana for written opinion with citation; don't execute electronically until written opinion confirms; keep existing drafts unsigned; resolve Crystal's contradictory statements about WillMaker Pro use.

## 2024-11-12: "tax exemption thresholds +5% from Jan 2025" per Diana Nov 9 (keywords: exemption threshold, 5%, Jan 2025, Diana, Montserrat tax)
- Crystal says Diana advised on 2024-11-09 that tax exemption thresholds rise 5% from January 2025. NOT verified; Montserrat thresholds unknown; unclear whether estate, gift, or inheritance tax, and whether any applies to Crystal.
- Earlier unverified claim: Christina/Crystal "12% above $200,000" (May 2 notes). Not confirmed.
- US context (if any US rules apply; from memory, not checked live): 2024 gift annual exclusion $18,000; 2025 reported as $19,000; federal estate exemption roughly $13.99M for 2025 (rise about 2.8%, not 5%). Verify with a tax adviser.
- Crystal's estate size (home ~$365k, savings, equipment, film rights, earning ~$85k) likely well below US federal exemption; whether the threshold matters depends on Montserrat rules.
- Advice: ask Diana for citation, which tax, threshold amounts, applicability to Crystal/parents/trust; don't change gifting or trust plans until confirmed; Christina to model the effect.

## 2024-11-12: increase gifts to kids without extra tax? (keywords: gifts to children, annual exclusion, minors, Jan 2025, not automatic)
- Crystal asks if the threshold change lets her increase gifts to kids without extra tax. Answer: no conclusion possible; threshold change unverified and Montserrat rules unknown. Any change would start Jan 2025 at earliest; 2024 gifts still under current rules.
- Distinction: the Aug 5 "10% increase" is a will provision (inheritance), not a gift; gifts during life are separate and have their own tax and legal consequences.
- Points: gift tax depends on jurisdiction; US 2024 annual exclusion $18,000 per recipient (2025 reported $19,000); gifts to minors need a trust or custodial arrangement (direct gifts give minors legal rights, guardianship/consent issues); gifts reduce Crystal's liquidity; records of each gift; equipment sale conflict unresolved; Christina and Diana to model before any increase.
- Advice: no increase until Diana confirms rules in writing and Christina models effect; keep gifts consistent with will and guardian/trust terms.

## 2024-11-12: 1Password implemented 2024-11-07 for digital estate credentials (keywords: 1Password, password manager, scams, emergency kit, secret key, recovery, version)
- Crystal implemented 1Password on 2024-11-07 to secure digital estate credentials; asks how it prevents scams and protects assets. Version not recorded (ask, per preference).
- Explained: strong unique passwords; autofill tied to matching sites (phishing protection); breach/weak-password alerts; secure storage of 2FA and recovery details; sharing/emergency access options (check current 1Password settings; not verified here).
- Limits: does not stop social engineering (fake attorney, bank, platform support asking for codes), malware on device, or someone tricking you into approving login prompts. Attorneys and executors should not need your master password.
- Critical: master password and Secret Key/Emergency Kit must be stored safely (safe) and separately; loss may make vault unrecoverable. Do not put master password in will or binder.
- Access for executor: sealed letter outside will with instructions; limit to trusted person; avoid giving Douglas/Kevin/Stephanie full control given conflicts. 2FA recovery codes should not live only in the vault.
- Red flags: anyone (including family, Stephanie, Kevin, Douglas) asking for vault or password details by email/phone.

## 2024-11-12: finalize will with Diana before Dec 15; Estate Tax Planning workshop Nov 2 (keywords: Dec 15, deadline, workshop, deductions, credits, prioritize)
- Crystal wants to finalize will with Diana before Stephanie's retirement (March 2025) and has a self-set deadline of 2024-12-15. Worried about time, and still processing workshop content (deductions/credits) from 2024-11-02 "Estate Tax Planning" workshop.
- Explained: Dec 15 is a personal target, not legal; Stephanie's retirement is March 2025; priority is a valid signed will, not speed. Workshop is general education; deductions and credits may not apply in Montserrat; check jurisdiction; bring questions to Diana.
- Prioritized list given: (1) Diana confirms e-signature and execution method in writing; (2) remove access codes from all drafts; (3) confirm guardianship nominees' written acceptance and Montserrat affidavit requirements; (4) confirm Aug 5/Nov 1/Nov 5 changes and percentages total 100% with residue clause; (5) care fund sizing and trust decision with tax memo; (6) binder and beneficiary designations match; (7) execution with two independent witnesses (non-beneficiaries); (8) custody and revocation of old versions.
- Advice: don't rush execution to meet Dec 15; if items unresolved, move signing date rather than sign an unverified version.

## 2024-11-12: do beneficiaries need updating when new digital assets are added? (keywords: beneficiary designation, digital inventory, digital clause, future assets)
- Explained: beneficiary designations apply to specific accounts/policies, not to digital assets generally. New digital assets fall under the will's digital clause and executor authority, unless the platform/account offers its own beneficiary/legacy option (then set it there).
- Assets with money value (payouts, royalty accounts, company shares, crypto if any) should be added to the separate inventory and checked against the will's percentages. Adding an asset to the inventory doesn't change the will; a change to terms, percentages, or named beneficiaries requires a new signed and witnessed version.
- Keep the digital inventory outside the will (will becomes public in probate); update it when assets change; access details in 1Password, not in inventory.
- Advice: ask Diana whether a digital clause that covers "all digital assets, present and future" is enough in Montserrat; confirm with Diana in writing.

## 2024-11-12: prioritize care fund ($7,000, "Bradley suggested Nov 1") vs digital legacy (Nov 5) before Dec 15; e-signature "required" (keywords: priority, Bradley, $7,000, required vs accepted, correction)
- Crystal says Bradley suggested the $7,000 care fund on 2024-11-01. Earlier record: Crystal said she added the fund herself on Nov 1. Clarify who proposed it and whether Bradley was consulted on amount.
- Correction: Crystal says Diana confirmed Montserrat "requires" e-signatures. Earlier record says Diana said Montserrat "accepts" them. Accepted is not required. Get written opinion stating the requirement and citation; a requirement would also mean paper signing may no longer be an option.
- Priority advice: the care fund sizing and trust decision carries the most consequence for parents but needs parents' facts and Christina's tax memo; digital legacy ($800) is low value and mostly governed by platform settings and the executor clause. Neither should block signing. Core must-haves: valid execution method, guardian acceptances, percentages totaling 100% with residue clause, no access codes in will.
- Option: if care amount unresolved by Dec 15, sign without a fixed figure only if Diana confirms it is valid; otherwise defer signing rather than sign an unsized fund. Digital legacy: keep general clause, details in inventory and 1Password.

## 2024-11-12: chose Diana (Nov 8) over Scott (Stephanie's referral); $900 vs $1,200 retainer (keywords: Diana, Scott, retainer, fee, independence, engagement letter)
- Crystal chose Diana on 2024-11-08 for "tech expertise"; Scott recommended by Stephanie. Fee: Diana $900 vs Scott $1,200 retainer. Not yet recorded: Diana's Montserrat admission, estate/probate experience, independence (relationship to Stephanie, Kevin, Douglas, Dwayne), engagement letter, whether fee is total or retainer.
- Points: tech expertise is not the main criterion; need Montserrat admission, estate and guardianship experience, written opinion ability, conflict check. Stephanie's referral of Scott is itself not independent; check Scott's credentials and any link to Stephanie. Retainer and fee are not comparable until total cost and scope are known.
- Diana's Nov 10 statement ("accepts" vs "requires" e-signatures) needs written citation.
- Advice: confirm Diana's credentials and independence in writing; get engagement letter in Crystal's name; compare total estimated cost and scope with Scott; choose on qualifications and independence, not price alone.

## 2024-11-12: guarantees/warranties from Diana vs Scott (keywords: guarantee, warranty, professional indemnity, liability, engagement letter)
- Crystal asks whether Diana offers guarantees or warranties like Scott "mentioned." Scott's statement not verified; no record of what either offered. Diana's terms unknown.
- Points: attorneys generally cannot guarantee outcomes (e.g., that a court will approve); usual protections are professional indemnity insurance, written scope, redo of work at no extra fee for errors they make, and fee refund terms. Confirm Montserrat requirements and terms in writing.
- Advice: request written engagement terms from Diana and Scott, including scope, liability/insurance confirmation, redo policy, fee refund terms, termination; compare the two in writing.

## 2024-11-12: does Diana's service agreement cover revising will for new laws? (keywords: service agreement, law changes, review, re-execution, scope)
- Crystal asks whether Diana's service agreement includes revising the will if new laws are enacted. Agreement not in record; no copy provided. Unknown.
- Points: engagement letters often limit scope to the work listed; updating a will for law changes is usually a separate engagement, often at extra fee; any revision needs re-execution (signed and witnessed) to take effect; law changes may affect will only in some cases; Montserrat-specific review timing unknown.
- Advice: ask Diana for the written service agreement; ask whether a review for law changes is included, its frequency, and fee for a new version; get the answer in writing.

## 2024-11-12: accepted Diana's $900 fee; how to proceed (keywords: engagement, roadmap, Diana, execution, witnesses, checklist)
- Crystal accepted Diana's $900 fee and asks how to proceed toward a legally valid will, noting she resisted Scott's higher fee. Fee should not be the deciding factor; confirm Diana's admission, independence, engagement letter, scope, insurance, written e-signature citation.
- Roadmap given (no time estimates): (1) signed engagement letter with scope and total fee; (2) written credentials and independence confirmation; (3) hand over Stephanie file and handover note; (4) written instructions on what each document must say; (5) confirm e-signature rule and execution method in writing; (6) guardian written acceptances; affidavit requirements; (7) settle percentages, residue, care fund, trust decision (after tax memo); (8) remove access codes; digital clause general; (9) binder and beneficiary designations matched; (10) execution: witnesses non-beneficiaries, custody, revocation of prior versions; (11) keep executor file and letter of wishes.

## 2024-11-12: does Diana's service include setting up e-signatures? (keywords: e-signature setup, scope, platform, witnesses, identity)
- Unknown: Diana's scope for e-signature setup not in record. Distinguish legal advice (whether e-signature valid, witnessing rules) from technical setup (platform, identity verification, audit trail, storage).
- Advice: ask Diana in writing whether setup is included, which platform, who pays platform fees, who holds the signing account, who verifies identity and witnesses; no signing until legal opinion confirmed.

## 2024-11-12: does Diana recommend a platform or can Crystal choose any secure one? (keywords: platform, recommendation, criteria, e-signature provider)
- Unknown whether Diana recommends a platform. Advice: do not pick one until Diana confirms legal requirements in writing; ask her for approved platforms and criteria; general e-signature tools are not automatically valid for wills; check audit trail, identity verification, witness support, export of final copy, data location, retention, access for executor.
- Note: WillMaker Pro and any digital drafting tool are drafting aids, not execution platforms unless Diana confirms.

## 2024-11-12: Kimberly's discomfort with digital assets in will; "clear instructions" given Nov 4 (keywords: Kimberly, digital discomfort, reassure, plain language, Nov 4)
- Crystal worried about Kimberly's discomfort with digital assets in the will; asks for help reassuring her with clear instructions "like I did on November 4." Nov 4 instructions not in record; ask Crystal to share them.
- Context: Kimberly (parent, beneficiary at 10% in earlier draft) previously preferred Kevin as executor; earlier advice: family told only after execution confirmed; say plan still being finalized.
- Advice: validate concern; explain digital section in plain language (what it does: lets executor manage accounts; what it doesn't: no passwords in will, no money transfers by will); share a summary, not the will text with codes or drafts; invite questions; parents decide their own wills/POA; suggest Kimberly may have her own adviser; avoid pressuring; record her concerns.

## 2024-11-12: Douglas booked 3-night stay at "Seaside Retreat" Nov 11 to celebrate will progress (keywords: Douglas, gift, appreciation, conflict, executor)
- Crystal asks how to show appreciation for the surprise. Douglas is executor and a possible beneficiary (20% in earlier draft). Gift or gesture is personal, separate from will; should not change will terms; no will provisions in exchange for gifts; record gifts received; disclose to Diana if will benefits him are changed.

## 2024-11-12: e-signatures for will updates + "new probate e-filing system, 20% faster" per Diana (keywords: e-filing, probate court, 20%, unverified, preference paper)
- Crystal prefers e-signatures for will updates to save time and paper. Asks how this works with a "new probate e-filing system" Diana explained, said to cut processing time 20%. Neither the e-filing system nor the 20% figure is verified; no record in notes of Diana saying this. Ask for citation, system name, effective date, and which court.
- Advice: preference does not override legal requirements; each update still needs valid execution per Diana's written opinion; e-filing (if real) is a court-process question, separate from will validity; don't rely on a speed figure; Montserrat probate timelines still unverified.

## 2024-11-12: repeat question: e-filing system "launched Oct 2024", 20% faster (keywords: e-filing, October 2024, unverified, repeat)
- Same question repeated. Launch date (Oct 2024) also unverified. No record Diana said it. Answer unchanged: ask Diana for system name, court, legal source, effective date in writing; e-filing does not establish will validity; preference doesn't override execution rules.

## 2024-11-12: $1,000 crypto wallets transfer instructions added Nov 6 (keywords: cryptocurrency, seed phrase, private keys, executor access, Nov 6)
- Crystal worried about transferring $1,000 crypto wallets to beneficiaries; asks to understand Nov 6 instructions. Text of Nov 6 instructions NOT in record; ask Crystal to share (no secrets pasted into chat; describe structure only).
- General points: loss of keys/seed phrase = permanent loss; no bank to contact; seed phrases and private keys must never be in will or any shared document; executor needs a sealed access method (secure location, instructions) outside will; list wallet type, exchange/custodian, approximate value date, tax status; check whether custodial exchanges offer beneficiary/legacy options; Montserrat legal status of crypto and tax unverified; Diana to review; ensure distribution method is possible for named beneficiaries (minors via trust).

## 2024-11-12: inform beneficiaries before crypto transfer? (keywords: beneficiaries, notice, crypto, confidentiality, minors)
- Generally no legal requirement to pre-notify beneficiaries of a will's contents (Montserrat unverified; ask Diana). Practical: do not share access details; executor and trustee/guardian for minors need to know the asset exists; beneficiaries need only what affects them; avoid telling beneficiaries about access methods; tell family only after execution, per earlier advice.

## 2024-11-12: must beneficiaries be told exact crypto amount beforehand? (keywords: crypto value, fluctuates, expectations, percentages)
- Not required; exact amounts fluctuate, so any figure is an estimate. Will should state shares as percentages or fixed amounts, with valuation date rule. Giving a number can create expectations and disputes. Share only that a share exists, not balances or access details. Confirm with Diana.

## 2024-11-12: 1Password setup tested with Natalie Nov 9; best way to keep digital assets secure (keywords: Natalie, 1Password test, shared access, rotate, 2FA, backup, watchtower)
- Crystal helped Natalie test 1Password on 2024-11-09 and feels good about sync. Concern: did Natalie see or get access to vault items during the test? If yes, remove her access and rotate any credential she saw. Natalie also suggested WillMaker Pro (2024-04-20).
- Security steps: strong master password and Secret Key/emergency kit stored in safe, separately; 2FA on 1Password account using authenticator app (not SMS); 2FA on email (email controls account recovery); printed recovery codes in safe; keep devices updated and locked; Watchtower checks; review sharing list quarterly; avoid unencrypted exports/screenshots; test emergency access with trusted person only after will; record app versions (preference).

## 2024-11-12: tracking estate-related expenses, $350 so far (keywords: expenses, receipts, planning costs vs probate costs, net estate, liquidity)
- Crystal tracking estate-related expenses at $350; "close to finalizing" will. Breakdown not in record; ask for it. Known planning costs: Diana $900 fee (accepted); Scott's retainer not engaged.
- Distinguish: planning costs paid now by Crystal (reduce her cash; not estate expenses); probate/administration costs paid later from estate (reduce net estate, which percentages apply to). Keep receipts for both; ask Christina whether any planning costs are deductible (jurisdiction unverified).
- Will should include clause on who pays estate expenses and from which assets; percentages apply to net estate after debts and expenses.
- "Close to finalizing" is not the same as ready: execution still depends on Diana's written e-signature opinion, guardian acceptances, and settled percentages.

## 2024-11-12: include the $350 planning expenses as a separate will section? (keywords: will clause, debts, expenses, receipts, binder)
- Advice: do not list past planning costs in will; will should have general clause for debts, taxes, funeral and administration expenses and who pays from which assets; past receipts go in binder/records. Diana to draft; confirm wording.

## 2024-11-12: will signing ceremony Dec 14, Montserrat Legal Center, 12 Queen's Rd (keywords: signing ceremony, Dec 14, venue, witnesses, checklist, not verified)
- Ceremony scheduled 2024-12-14 at "Montserrat Legal Center, 12 Queen's Rd." Venue and address NOT verified; confirm it is Diana's practice or a real, accessible location.
- Prerequisites not yet complete per record: Diana written e-signature opinion (paper vs electronic); guardian written acceptances (Stephanie, Kevin); percentages total 100% + residue clause; care fund decision; Stephanie handover; access codes removed from all drafts; beneficiary designations matched; revocation clause; affidavit requirements.
- Witnesses: two independent adults, not beneficiaries, executors, guardians (Douglas, Kevin, Stephanie, Dwayne excluded); confirm witness rules with Diana.
- Checklist: final printed version reviewed; no drafts or codes brought; ID; original custody decided; copies marked; notary only if Diana requires for other documents; decide whether ceremony is paper or electronic.
- Advice: ceremony date is before Dec 15 target; if prerequisites incomplete, reschedule rather than sign.

## 2024-11-12: monthly estate-related expenses raised to $420 (keywords: budget, monthly, legal consultations, cash flow, care fund, not from children's money)
- Crystal raised monthly estate-related expenses to $420 due to more legal consultations; earlier total was $350 (clarify: total vs monthly). Income ~ $85,000/yr (from profile; take-home unknown). Budget not in record; ask for income, fixed costs, debts, and current savings.
- Advice: treat planning costs as separate line; set a cap for legal spending before engagement; don't fund planning costs from care fund, children's money, or the parents' gifts; keep an emergency buffer; confirm Diana's billing (hourly or fixed) so costs are predictable; ask Christina to review cash flow and gifting plan; record receipts.

## User preference (2024-11-12): confirm attorney names and credentials whenever legal representation is discussed (keywords: preference, credentials, attorney names, verify)
- Crystal asks that attorney names and credentials always be confirmed when legal representation comes up. Assistant cannot independently verify credentials (no registry lookup done). Approach: state names as reported by Crystal, mark credentials as unverified, and give steps to verify (Montserrat bar/court registry, written credentials from attorney, references).
- Current attorneys on record: Diana (new, engaged, $900, credentials not yet verified in writing); Scott (Stephanie referral, $1,200 retainer, credentials unknown); Stephanie (retiring March 2025; credentials unknown).

## 2024-11-12: resources to learn estate tax minimization; contradiction on workshops (keywords: workshop contradiction, resources, IRS Pub 950, Montserrat government, learning)
- Crystal says she has never attended estate tax planning workshops or financial literacy events. CONTRADICTS Nov 2 "Estate Tax Planning" workshop she described earlier this month. Flag and ask which is correct and where the material came from.
- Resources suggested (not checked live): Diana (reading list, tailored to Montserrat); Christina (tax memo); Montserrat government and official tax/finance offices (verify current publications); local bar or law library; for US rules only if they apply: IRS Publication 950 (estate and gift tax) and Publication 559 (executors and administrators). Verify currency before relying.
- Advice: learning is fine, but minimization strategies must be chosen with Diana and Christina; no strategy implemented from general reading.

## 2025-02-20: user revisits 5% threshold worry (keywords: 2025-02-20, threshold, higher exemption, Dec 14 status unknown, Stephanie March)
- Crystal (2025-02-20) worried about the "+5% thresholds from Jan 2025" (Diana, Nov 9) and how it affects her plan, citing the Nov 5 digital legacy ($800 Instagram/TikTok).
- Key point given: a higher exemption threshold means LESS exposure to tax, not more; the worry needs reframing. Still unverified which tax and which jurisdiction.
